summary: A 182-item partial extraction preserving all prior IDs/statuses and the corrected absolute Weyl group and fibre product. The continuation constructs quasi-split ordinary classes and proves a quaternion inner-form counterexample, with a unique basic admissible class that is not ordinary. structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

qualifications: WittVector.isocrystal_classification assumes finrank exactly one; it does not supply Dieudonne-Manin in all ranks.
The reductive-group and torus predicates are built. Their rational Newton, sigma-conjugacy, local-global cohomology and Shimura interfaces are separate contracts.

The dominant-chamber uniqueness result is for a finite reduced crystallographic root system with the flipped pairing reduced and strictly ordered coefficients. The central torus and rational coroot cone adapters remain N05.
TauCeti.posRootCone in RootSystem/Positive.lean uses integral nonnegative coefficients. It does not by itself supply the rational dominance cone used here.
The abelian-variety and finite-surjective isogeny carriers are reused; the relative universal family, rational Hom tensor functor and isogeny torsors are additional contracts.
A divided-power structure is not a PD envelope, log site, convergent isocrystal or crystalline comparison theorem.
Proposed API wrappers on library items are not additional claims that their names or full contracts are implemented.

items.name: General rational-Levi minuscule lift (corrected: absolute Weyl group)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, M a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup, T⊂M a maximal torus, μ a minuscule cocharacter of M, and [b_M]∈B(M)_b such that ([b_M],{μ}) is G-admissible. Then there is w in the absolute Weyl group W(G,T)(Q̄_p), equivalently a G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T, such that ([b_M],{w·μ}) is M-admissible. The printed requirement w∈N_G(M)/M is false, by the GL₃ example with M=GL₁×GL₂, μ=(0,1,0), b_M=diag(p,1,1) (errata E2).
items.note: Corrected formulation and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026), following the structure of the paper's proof with the correct Weyl group. The only use, Corollary 1.1.17 (N32), needs exactly this: its proof writes "By Lemma 1.1.13, there exists w∈W(G,T)". The remaining inputs are N27 and its cited unramified result, and Kottwitz97 4.4, under G-local. The G-source gate for the normalizer statement is resolved by this correction.
proofSteps: Choose a rational parabolic P with Levi M and an inner twisting ξ:G→G* to the quasi-split form with ξ(P)=P* rational, as in the paper. Then ξ|_M:M→M* is an inner twisting, and B(M)_b≅π₁(M)_Γ=π₁(M*)_Γ≅B(M*)_b gives [b_{M*}].

Let μ* be the B*∩M*-dominant representative of ξ|_M∘μ. The pair ([b_{M*}],{μ*}) is G*-admissible. The κ-condition holds by functoriality of the Kottwitz maps and the compatible identifications π₁(M)=π₁(M*), π₁(G)=π₁(G*). The Newton condition holds because the Newton points of basic classes lie in X_*(A_{M*})_Q and are determined by κ ([Kot97, 4.4]). This is the paper's own argument.
Apply N27 (Proposition 1.1.13) to G*: there is w* in W(G*,T*), not only in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, with ([b_{M*}],{w*·μ*}) M*-admissible. The paper's proof misquotes this output as w*∈W(G*,M*).

Transport back along ξ, which identifies W(G,T)(Q̄_p) with W(G*,T*) after conjugating ξ(T) to T* inside M*. For basic b_M, M-admissibility of ([b_M],{μ′}) is the κ_M-equality κ_M(b_M)=μ′^♯ in π₁(M)_Γ (Lemma 1.1.6), which transports through π₁(M)=π₁(M*).

Its étale realization must be a global absolute-Hodge section; apply S10/A16 and A18 to extend it and detect identity, composition, tensor, dual and idempotent relations. This enlargement and the original absolute-Hodge input remain G-tensors.

Use tensor generation of finite-dimensional Rep(G) by a faithful V and char-zero reductive semisimplicity: every representation is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of mixed tensors. Split the transported idempotents in F-Isoc, descend morphisms through these summands, and verify independence of presentation and exact faithfulness with pointwise fiber functors. items.name: Rational abelian-quotient map
items.statement: There is a Q-group map I_x→G_ab whose base change equals the maps induced by i_ℓ for every ℓ. The auxiliary Shimura datum must be G′=G×_{G^ab}T, pairs (g,t) with the same image in G^ab, not the printed G×T.
items.note: Repair and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). With the printed G′=G×T the construction fails twice: G×T is not in GSp(V⊕V,ψ⊕ψ), and the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} contains 1×T, which maps onto G^ab. This is recorded in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22.json (E5). The remaining inputs, Corollary 2.1.9 and Noot, stay under G-noot.
proofSteps: For a special point (T,h_T) of (G,X) put G′=G×_{G^ab}T⊂G×T acting on V′=V⊕V, with T acting on the second copy through T⊂G. Similitude factors through G^ab, so G′⊂GSp(V′,ψ⊕ψ). Since h^ab is constant on X, X′=X×{h_T} maps into Hom(S,G′_R), giving an embedding of Shimura data (G′,X′)↪(GSp(V′),H′).

As in the paper, conjugating T→G by G^ad(Q), the point s₀ lifts to s′₀ on the integral model for (G′,X′). A_{s′₀} is isogenous to A_{s₀}×A_T, and I_{s′₀} preserves the decomposition. Restriction to A_T gives I_{s′₀}→T; compose with T→G^ab.

Kernel check: the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} (restriction to A_{s₀}) lies, after base change to any Q_ℓ, in ker(G′→G)={(1,t):t∈T∩G^der}. That kernel maps trivially to G^ab. So the composite kills ker(I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀}), and since I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} is surjective (Corollary 2.1.9) it factors through a Q-map I_{s₀}→G^ab.

Compatibility with i_ℓ: over Q_ℓ, the map I_{s₀}→G^ab so obtained and the composite I_{s₀}⊗Q_ℓ≅I_{ℓ,s₀}→G_{Q_ℓ}→G^ab_{Q_ℓ} agree on the image of I_{s′₀}, because for (g,t)∈G′ the images of g and t in G^ab coincide.

items.name: Torus Newton invariant is the Galois average
items.statement: For an F=Q_p torus T and λ∈X_*(T), let [b_T]=κ_T^{-1}([λ]). Then ν_T(b_T)=N_Γ λ in X_*(T)_Q^Γ. The average is rational; κ_T still retains integral coinvariant torsion.
proofSteps: Use the natural isomorphism X_*(T)_Γ→B(T) normalized by valuation one on G_m (Kottwitz85 §§2.2–2.5). For a finite Galois splitting field E/F and maximal unramified subfield E_0, a representative is N_{E/E_0}(λ(π_E))∈T(E_0)⊂T(L). The alternative finite splitting extension over L used by KMPS has the same normalization.

Pair with every F-rational character χ. The representative has valuation ⟨χ,λ⟩; the invariant rational cocharacter is uniquely determined by these pairings. Equivalently, Kottwitz85 (2.8.1) is precisely finite orbit averaging.

Kottwitz85 §4.4 identifies this valuation map with the tensorial Newton map. Thus the Newton formula follows without discarding κ torsion. The sign-action lattice has nonzero Z/2 coinvariant but zero rational average.

items.name: Ordinary class for a quasi-split group
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p quasi-split, any geometric cocharacter class {μ} has a unique [b_μ]∈B(G,{μ}) with ν=μ^diamond. Choose a Q_p-rational Borel pair T⊂B and B-dominant μ∈X_*(T). The image of κ_T^{-1}([μ]) has the required invariants. A rational Newton representative exists. This algebraic existence statement does not by itself prove density in an integral model.
items.locator: KMPS §1.3.15 corrected quasi-split scope; Kottwitz85 §§2.8,4.4,6.2; Kisin–Zhou arXiv:2103.09945v2 Remark 2.2.5
proofSteps: Choose the rational Borel pair supplied by quasi-split reductive-group theory, with T a maximal torus. The Galois action preserves the dominant chamber; averaging its finite orbit gives a dominant invariant rational cocharacter μ^diamond.
Send the torus class κ_T^{-1}([μ]) into B(G). Functoriality gives κ_G=μ^sharp and ν_G equal to the dominant orbit of N_Γ μ=μ^diamond. Hence it is admissible and attains the Hodge bound.

All other admissible classes have the same κ and smaller or equal ν. Equality gives equality of classes by N11. N16, with Kottwitz85 Proposition 6.2, supplies (1.1.3.1). The rational Borel-pair and general classification prerequisites are still part of G-local.

items.name: Quaternion division algebra and its split Frobenius model
items.statement: Fix F=Q_p, its unramified quadratic extension E with automorphism τ, and D=E⊕E j with j²=p and j a=τ(a)j. Then D is a division algebra. Over L=breve Q_p, identify D_L with M_2(L) by a↦diag(a,τa) and j↦J=[[0,p],[1,0]]. The F-descent operator is σ_D(A)=J σ(A) J^{-1}; σ_D²=σ². Put G=D^×.
items.locator: Worker-derived cyclic-algebra example for KMPS §1.3.15; split descent checked directly
proofSteps: The cyclic presentation has associative multiplication by j a=τ(a)j. Its conjugation sends a+bj to τ(a)−bj and gives norm N_E/F(a)−p N_E/F(b). For nonzero a,b the two summands have respectively even and odd p-adic valuations, so cannot cancel. If one vanishes the other does not. Every nonzero element has inverse conjugate/norm, proving division.

The displayed matrices satisfy the cyclic relations; over E their span is M_2(E), giving the splitting after base change. Apply σ entrywise, whose restriction to E is τ. Conjugation by J fixes the embedded a and j; it is therefore the descent action of D. Since σ(J)=J and J²=pI, its square is σ².

Use the units of the finite-dimensional central simple F-algebra for the algebraic group, not GL_2 with the untwisted Frobenius. Its quasi-split inner form is split GL_2. The local-field existence of E and general reductive inner-form interface are retained in G-local.

proofSteps: For c∈GL_2(L), compute (c b σ_D(c)^{-1})J=c(bJ)σ(c)^{-1}. Thus the bijection on matrices carries exactly the two equivalence relations, and multiplication by J^{-1} gives its inverse.
The reduced norm of b is det(b), so κ_D(b)=v_p(det b). The determinant of J is −p, yielding the shift by one. Do not equate inner-form κ values using this particular set bijection.

items.name: Half-slope shift for the quaternion inner twist
items.statement: For C03 and C04, if the ordinary GL_2-isocrystal (bJ)σ has dominant slopes (a,c), the dominant Newton vector for b with descent σ_D is (a−1/2,c−1/2).
items.locator: Derived from Kottwitz85 (4.3.1)–(4.3.3); KMPS (1.1.2.2) with corrected endpoint
proofSteps: For every even r, induction on the semilinear products gives ∏_{i=0}^{r−1}σ_D^i(b)=[∏_{i=0}^{r−1}σ^i(bJ)]J^{−r}=p^{−r/2}∏σ^i(bJ). Odd r has a noncentral factor J^{−r}, so evenness matters.

Choose an even common multiple of the decency exponent for b. If c makes b decent, then it makes bJ σ-conjugate by the same c. Since σ_D^r(c)=σ^r(c), the preceding equality remains valid after the conjugation. The GL_2 decency cocharacter is ν_D+(1/2,1/2).

Uniqueness of the Newton cocharacter from the decency characterization (Kottwitz85 §§4.3–4.4) gives the asserted shift. For b=1 the GL_2 class of J has slopes (1/2,1/2), whereas ν_D(1)=0; this checks the normalization.

items.name: Two distinct rank-two slopes are integral
items.statement: For a two-dimensional isocrystal over Frac W(Fpbar), two distinct slopes must both be integers. Each distinct slope space has dimension one. This consequence uses the rank-one classification and slope decomposition, not a claim that all-rank classification exists in Mathlib.
items.locator: Kottwitz85 §3 and §4.2; pinned Mathlib WittVector.isocrystal_classification, lines 183–185
proofSteps: The slope decomposition is Frobenius-stable and the two nonzero summands have dimensions summing to two, hence each has dimension one.

Apply WittVector.isocrystal_classification to each summand with its verified finrank-one hypothesis. Its standard Frobenius is p^m σ for an integer m, so each slope is integral. The decomposition adapter comes from VB0; it is not an existing Mathlib theorem about arbitrary rank.

items.name: Quaternion obstruction to an ordinary class
items.statement: For G=D^× from C03 and any integer m, let {μ_m} have split dominant representative (m+1,m). Then B(G,{μ_m}) has no class with Newton vector μ_m^diamond=(m+1,m). In particular μ=(1,0) and the inverse-Hodge class represented dominantly by (0,−1) both fail ordinary existence.
proofSteps: The quasi-split inner form is split GL_2, so the based Galois action is trivial and the Hodge average is (m+1,m). These cocharacters are minuscule.
If a class attained this vector, C05 would give ordinary GL_2 slopes (m+3/2,m+1/2). They are distinct and nonintegral, contradicting C06.

For the positive example take m=0; for the inverse-Hodge example take m=−1. The obstruction is local and refutes unconditional inner-form existence in §1.3.15. No global Shimura realization, no claim about the final Duke text, and no counterexample to the additional local-integrality hypothesis of Corollary 1.3.16 is inferred.

items.name: A unique maximal admissible class need not be ordinary
items.statement: For C07, B(D^×,{μ_m}) is a singleton. Its representative is b=p^m J and its Newton vector is (m+1/2,m+1/2), strictly below μ_m^diamond. Thus its unique greatest class is basic and is not μ-ordinary.
proofSteps: The proposed b lies in D^×(F), has κ_D=2m+1, and bJ=p^{m+1}I. C05 gives ν_D=(m+1/2,m+1/2); its difference from μ_m is one half of the positive GL_2 coroot, so it is admissible.

For any other admissible b, let a≥c be the slopes of (bJ)σ. Their sum is 2m+2 by C04. Admissibility gives a−1/2≤m+1, hence a≤m+3/2. If a≠c, both are integers by C06, forcing a≤m+1; with a≥c and fixed sum this forces a=c=m+1, a contradiction.
Hence all admissible classes have a=c=m+1 and the same κ. N11 identifies them. This gives a complete local distinction between a greatest admissible class and attainment of the Hodge average.

items.name: Rational cocharacters of a division algebra are central
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional division algebra D/F, every F-morphism λ:G_m→D^× is λ(t)=t^n·1 for an integer n. Every rational F-defined cocharacter is central. In C03 the basic class C08 has a rational Newton representative, but the noncentral orbit (m+1,m) has none.
proofSteps: An algebraic map into the finite-dimensional affine space D is a finite Laurent polynomial λ(t)=Σ a_n t^n. The identity λ(st)=λ(s)λ(t) implies a_n²=a_n and a_n a_k=0 for n≠k. Also Σa_n=1.
A division algebra has only idempotents 0 and 1. Exactly one a_n is 1 and all others vanish. Thus λ(t)=t^n. Clear a positive denominator for a rational cocharacter.
For b=p^m J, σ_D(b)=b and b²=p^{2m+1}I; the Newton map is the rational central cocharacter (m+1/2,m+1/2), defined over F. This verifies the witness condition independently of ordinary existence.

items.name: Ordinary Newton class with an explicit witness
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p and a cocharacter class {μ}, OrdinaryClass(G,{μ}) consists of an actual [b]∈B(G), the equality κ_G(b)=μ^sharp and the equality ν_G(b)=μ^diamond. It is a subsingleton by N11 and can be empty. A rational Newton representative is separate data required by the geometric nonemptiness theorem.
proofSteps: Construct the subtype of classes satisfying both equalities. The ν equality implies the admissibility inequality by reflexivity. Injectivity of (κ,ν) proves any two inhabitants equal.

C02 supplies an inhabitant for quasi-split G. C07 supplies a genuine empty example. Do not implement a total constructor indexed only by G and μ, or identify the greatest admissible class with an inhabitant.

sourceIssues.correction: Take G′ = G ×_{G^ab} T, the pairs (g, t) with the same image in G^ab. This lies in GSp(V ⊕ V, ψ ⊕ ψ), and X′ = X × {h_T} still maps into it because h^ab is constant on X. The kernel of G′ → G is T ∩ G^der, which dies in G^ab, so the composite I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab does factor through I_{s_0}. The rest of the proof then goes through.
sourceIssues.reason: Read literally, the construction fails at two points. First, G × T acting on V ⊕ V does not preserve ψ ⊕ ψ up to a scalar when the similitude factors of g and t differ, so it is not a subgroup of G_{V′}. Second, the claimed factorization fails. The CM automorphisms (1, t), t ∈ T, act trivially on A_{s_0} and by t on A_T, and they preserve the tensors cutting out G × T. So 1 × T lies in I_{s′_0}, and also in the kernel of I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0}. But under I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab it maps onto G^ab, as T is a maximal torus of G. So the map does not factor through I_{s_0} unless G^ab = 1. The same happens over Q_ℓ, so the justification "as this is true over Q_ℓ" fails too. Surjectivity of I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0} alone cannot give a factorization. What is needed is that the kernel maps trivially, and the fibre product above provides this. Lemma 2.2.8 is used in the proof of Proposition 2.2.2 (p.28). Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 7, item T23) as a descent gate; the analysis and the fibre-product repair are given here.
